deduped_items.body_text:
Prosecution says journalists’ testimony indicates Matsda2sh was ‘Brotherhood media cell,’ EIPR says statement unproven position          
The Public Prosecution issued a statement on Wednesday regarding the investigations into the six Matsda2sh fact-checking platform’s journalists, stating that one of them admitted that all the defendants — as well as others — had joined a media committee affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood.
It said they had been tasked with carrying out “media plans” based on spreading and broadcasting rumors and false news about state institutions, exclusively highlighting the shortcomings of those institutions, disparaging the roles and performance of their officials and overblowing issues related to select groups, as well as fabricating and exaggerating events related to them.
From its side, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose lawyers are leading the defense counsel representing the journalists, repeated its demands for their release, for the charges against them to be dropped and for the case to be closed.
In response to the prosecution’s statement, EIPR said that its media statements published on social media hold no evidentiary value in law and amount only to a summary of the prosecution’s case, none of which has been presented before a court, while none of its claims has been proven.
The organization pointed out the prosecution’s failure to address the fact that the six journalists did not appear before the prosecution until five days after their arrest, during which time they were denied contact with their families and lawyers, in violation of the law, despite relatives and lawyers filing 18 complaints with the prosecution during that period.
The prosecution’s statement also failed to mention that the order to hold the journalists in custody is issued by investigating authorities under the exceptional provisions of the counterterrorism law, which only permit the measure “when there is a threat of terrorist crimes and when such measure is required to confront that threat,” according to EIPR.
Yet the prosecution’s claims, based on the security investigations, accuse the journalists only of publishing rumors or “false” reports, without identifying “the imminent terrorist threat that required depriving the six journalists of their right to appear before a judicial authority within 24 hours of their arrest, during which documented violations were committed against them.”
The six journalists appeared before the prosecutions five days after their forced disappearance following their arrest, during which they were held at National Security Agency premises.
None were brought before prosecutors until the first of the six was presented to the Supreme State Security Prosecution on Saturday, with the other five interrogated on the following day. The prosecution ordered that one of the six be brought for forensic medical examination, after some of the defendants complained of being subjected to torture and maltreatment at the NSA premises, with lawyers calling for officers responsible for those premises to be investigated.
The prosecution stated that the first journalist who was investigated admitted that the defendants received “monthly funding of sums in foreign currencies,” via bank transfers from a company owned by a “fugitive member of the Muslim Brotherhood” in a foreign country.
The prosecution also said it found communication groups on a secure messaging app on his phone, connecting him and the other detainees with the “fugitive member,” as well as emails from the latter to them. All but one admitted to regularly receiving sums of money in US dollars, transferred from a foreign country.
After the statement’s publication, EIPR director, Hossam Bahgat, told Mada Masr that the prosecution is pointing to the procedural steps Matsda2sh took to regularize as though it were incriminating evidence. deduped_items.body_text:
RSF preps new front from Ethiopia, pummels Blue Nile; In Kordofan, RSF conducts ‘field’ executions, digs in heels at Nuhud; Dagris prison dispute stalls registry; Gov’t criticizes UN fact-finding renewal          
With all eyes turned toward the escalating conflict in Ethiopia that is teetering on the brink of becoming a wider regional war, the Rapid Support Forces stepped up their attacks on the Sudan war’s southeastern front this week.
Blue Nile’s Wad al-Mahi locality in the east of the state bore the brunt of the escalation. The RSF launched an attack from Ethiopia on Saturday and seized the Kadalo mountains area, which sits near the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam and Roseires Dam reservoir. This coincided with a drone campaign against Damazin, which included strikes on the homes of Blue Nile Governor Ahmed Badry and Regional Finance Minister Abbas Kara, fuel stations, military sites, universities and mosques.
The military has hit back, launching airstrikes on RSF positions in Wad al-Mahi and tried to reassure residents. As of Sunday, about 2,800 people are estimated to have been displaced from 10 villages in Wad al-Mahi.
But action in the southeastern front wasn’t limited to the Blue Nile. Large numbers of RSF fighters have been moved from Darfur to Addis Ababa in recent weeks in preparation to transfer them toward Sudan’s eastern border, where they are expected to gear up for an attack on the Fashaga border strip in Gadarif State, according to an RSF source and another source informed of the mobilization arrangements who spoke to Mada Masr.
In anticipation of escalating attacks on the border, the Sudanese military has reinforced its positions in the east, military sources tell Mada Masr. And on Wednesday, military chief and Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan visited the 11th Infantry Division in Khashm al-Gerba, Kassala State, which borders Gadarif to the north.
On the western front, the military is preparing to attack the remaining RSF-held areas in North Kordofan and advance into West Kordofan, with eyes set on Um Bader and Hamra al-Sheikh in northwestern North Kordofan. Meanwhile, the RSF is digging its heels in West Kordofan, with the group having dug trenches and built earth berms around the strategic city of Nuhud to guard against surprise attacks, an activist in the state told Mada Masr.
West Kordofan also saw yet another attack on an aid truck this week, with Khartoum laying blame for the strike at the feet of the RSF and the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (Abdel Aziz al-Hilu faction).
In Um Bader, a social media video of the execution of 23 detainees is raising concern. While the RSF-led Tasis government tried to pin the executions on the military, three sources from the paramilitary group confirmed that the RSF had carried out the ‘field’ executions. As to why, the RSF sources’ accounts conflicted with those of medical sources and relatives of one of the men killed who spoke to Mada Masr. But both Tasis and officials in Khartoum are keen to pursue justice, even if a Tasis official continued to dismiss the RSF’s implications when presented with what sources from the paramilitary told Mada Masr.
In Darfur, the joint forces push toward Geneina continues to stall, with territory swapping hands. The US’s politicking over the Darfur arms embargo — which has done next to nothing to stop the flow of weapons through Darfur or seen the provider of those arms in the United Arab Emirates face international criticism — got kicked down the road for another two months, as DC continues its push to extend the embargo across the whole country. The UN’s fact-finding committee on Sudan did get its mandate renewed, much to the chagrin of the government in Khartoum, which sees any form of international intervention as an infringement on its sovereignty. And opacity around the infamous Dagris prison, where an estimated 20,000 people are being detained, has posed a roadblock in the government-RSF p

deduped_items.title: Названа причина досрочного завершения переговоров США и Украины в Майами
deduped_items.body_text:
Переговоры США и Украины в Майами досрочно завершились из-за соглашения Москвы и Вашингтона о поставках российского дизельного топлива. Об этом передает газета Financial Times (FT) со ссылкой на источники.
«Но эта встреча была сорвана, когда украинская команда была застигнута врасплох заявлением Трампа о том, что он заключил сделку с [президентом России] Владимиром Путиным по поставке дизельного топлива», — говорится в материале.
10 октября журналист Алекс Рауфоглу сообщил, что переговоры США и Украины в Майами завершились досрочно. Он отметил, что запланированный второй день переговоров не состоится.
Ранее президент России Владимир Путин заявил, что Москва готова поставлять нефть и нефтепродукты на американский и мировой рынки. Он отметил, что такой шаг «положительно отразится на всей глобальной экономике».

deduped_items.title: Лидерами по рождаемости в России стали Тува и Чечня
deduped_items.body_text:
Самые высокие показатели рождаемости в России демонстрируют такие национальные республики, как Тува, Чечня, Ингушетия и Алтай. Об этом со ссылкой на исследование Агентства стратегических инициатив (АСИ), основанное на данных Росстата, сообщает РИА Новости.
Аналитический доклад об изменениях в здравоохранении, образовании, инфраструктуре и городской среде связан с национальным рейтингом качества жизни за 2025 год, который АСИ ежегодно готовит по поручению президента России Владимира Путина.
В нем, в частности, учитываются три показателя — это число рождений на тысячу женщин фертильного возраста (15-49 лет) и возрастные коэффициенты рождаемости в возрастных группах 30-34 года и 35-39 лет, то есть число рождений на 1000 женщин соответствующего возраста.
В среднем по стране первый показатель равен 35,9, второй — 66,5, а третий — 38,4. Тува и Чечня входят в тройку лидеров по каждому из них. Ингушетия оказалась среди лучших по общему показателю рождаемости, а также по рождаемости в возрасте 35-39 лет. В возрастной категории 30-34 года ее место заняла Республика Алтай.
Ранее вице-премьер России Татьяна Голикова назвала демографическую ситуацию в России непростой, но подконтрольной. В свою очередь, Путин похвалил руководство Чечни за высокую рождаемость.

deduped_items.title: «Урал» проиграл «Велесу» и прервал беспроигрышную серию
deduped_items.body_text:
«Урал» проиграл московскому «Велесу» со счетом 1:2 в домашнем матче 13-го тура Первой лиги. Об этом сообщает «Спорт-Экспресс».
Гости забили два мяча в первом тайме. На 16-й минуте защитник «Урала» Дмитрий Тихой срезал мяч в свои ворота, а на 23-й минуте Артур Колосков реализовал пенальти. Во втором тайме защитник Сильвие Бегич на 66-й минуте сократил отставание, но отыграться екатеринбуржцы не смогли.
Для «Урала» это второе поражение в сезоне. Команда прервала серию из 11 матчей без поражений. «Велес» одержал первую победу за пять матчей.
После 13 туров «Урал» занимает третье место с 25 очками. «Велес» поднялся на вторую строчку с 26 очками после 14 игр. Лидирует «Нижний Новгород» с 31 очком. Следующий матч «Урал» проведет 18 октября в Екатеринбурге против «Нижнего Новгорода».

deduped_items.title: В Приамурье ищут пенсионерку, пропавшую пять дней назад
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- В Амурской области ведутся поиски 70-летней женщины, пропавшей пять дней назад в поселке Архара.
- Поисковики нашли следы, ведущие в поле площадью 132 гектара, но пока не смогли обнаружить женщину.
- К поискам в воскресенье планируют подключить параплан, если позволит погода.
УЛАН-УДЭ, 10 окт - РИА Новости. Поиски пожилой женщины, пропавшей пять дней назад в местах, где обитают медведи и тигры, ведутся в Амурской области, сообщила РИА Новости руководитель поисково-спасательный отряда "Амур" Татьяна Шалашова. 
По данным отряда, 70-летняя женщина пропала в поселке Архара. Последний раз она выходила на связь с родными в понедельник, с тех пор ее телефон недоступен. 
Эксперт рассказал, что делать при встрече с медведем в городе29 августа, 01:15
«
"Шестого числа нам заявка (о пропаже пенсионерки - ред.) пришла. По дороге в сторону Орловки мы нашли следы, ведущие в поле. Чтобы вы понимали, поле там 132 гектара. По метру-сантиметру мы шли, следы довели нас до кустов. Они очень высокие. Дальше уже выхода из этих кустов нет. Пока найти не можем", - рассказала собеседница агентства. 
При этом, она отметила, что следы медведей, тигра - это обычное явление для этой местности. 
"Там живет медведица с медвежатами в том месте. И это ареал обитания тигров. Это их, как говорится, территория. Поэтому обнаруживать там следы - это ничего сверхъестественного. Это таежная местность, они там живут. И местные жители об этом знают", - добавила Шалашова. 
Также она подчеркнула, что в воскресенье, если позволит погода, к поискам подключат параплан.
Эксперт рассказала, как вести себя при встрече с медведем19 августа, 15:30

deduped_items.title: Митрополия в Черногории подтвердила запрос на съемку от команды Звинчука
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Митрополия Черногорско-Приморская Сербской православной церкви подтвердила получение запроса от авторов проекта "Рыбарь" на проведение съемки в монастыре.
- Михаил Звинчук и его коллеги были задержаны в Черногории, а позже выдворены из страны.
БЕЛГРАД, 10 окт – РИА Новости. Митрополия Черногорско-Приморская Сербской православной церкви подтвердила получение запроса от авторов проекта "Рыбарь" на проведение съемки в монастыре накануне задержания в пятницу. 
Михаил Звинчук, его супруга Валерия и трое их коллег были задержаны в городе Рисан в Черногории. Позже МВД республики сообщило, что принято решение о выдворении россиян. Вечером в пятницу он прибыл самолетом в Белград и сообщил, что перед задержанием отправил запрос на съемки в монастыре Пресвятой Богородицы в городе Цетине. 
"Так как запрос на проведение съемок поступил накануне прибытия в монастырь, вне рабочего времени, мы его не успели рассмотреть. На следующий день мы узнали из СМИ, что лица, обратившиеся к нам с этим запросом, задержаны полицией", - говорится в заявлении Митрополии Черногорско-Приморской. 
Посольство России в Черногории ранее заявило РИА Новости, что потребовало у черногорской стороны разъяснить причины задержания Звинчука и других российских граждан, а также обеспечить к ним консульский доступ.

deduped_items.title: МИД: контакт Меланьи Трамп по ситуации в Алешках покажет США факты
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Посол по особым поручениям МИД РФ Родион Мирошник считает, что прямой контакт аппарата Меланьи Трамп с уполномоченным по правам человека в России Яной Лантратовой по ситуации в Алешках Херсонской области предоставит Вашингтону объективные факты о происходящем в городе.
- Родион Мирошник отметил, что контакты с американской стороной могут разрушить украинский мифический нарратив, который Киев пытается выносить на международные площадки.
- Пресс-секретарь президента России Дмитрий Песков заявил, что Вооруженные силы РФ делают все, чтобы решить проблему поставок продуктов и медикаментов в Алешки в Херсонской области, которым сейчас препятствует Киев.
МОСКВА, 10 окт - РИА Новости. Прямой контакт аппарата первой леди США Меланьи Трамп с уполномоченным по правам человека в России Яной Лантратовой по ситуации в Алешках Херсонской области предоставит Вашингтону объективные факты о происходящем в городе, считает посол по особым поручениям МИД РФ Родион Мирошник. 
Ранее Лантратова заявила, что находится на связи с американской стороной и командой Меланьи Трамп по ситуации в Алешках. 
"Прямой контакт с аппаратом Мелании Трамп позволит предоставить Вашингтону объективные факты о происходящем в Алешках", - пишет газета ВЗГЛЯД со ссылкой на слова Мирошника. 
Он отметил, что контакты гарантированно могут разрушить украинский мифический нарратив, который Киев пытается выносить на международные площадки. 
"Как минимум, это выбьет одного из западных партнеров Украины, который если и не поддерживал, то спокойно относился к преступлениям украинской стороны. Настроение США при получении детализированной и понятной информации может измениться", - добавил дипломат. 
Ранее пресс-секретарь президента России Дмитрий Песков заявил, что Вооруженные силы РФ делают все, чтобы решить проблему поставок продуктов и медикаментов в Алешки в Херсонской области, которым сейчас препятствует Киев. Он подчеркнул, что ситуация там критическая, так как Украина делает все, чтобы помешать этим поставкам. 
Алешки находятся на левом берегу Днепра напротив подконтрольного ВСУ города Херсон. Ранее губернатор Херсонской области Владимир Сальдо сообщал, что ВСУ дистанционно минируют подъездные дороги и атакуют дронами транспорт, пытаясь заблокировать поставки продуктов, топлива и медикаментов, а также наносят удары по объектам энергетики и связи города, чтобы создать сложную гуманитарную ситуацию.

deduped_items.title: Brunori show, monologhi e canzoni. “La sinistra lontana dal paese, nero come un caffè di cicoria”
deduped_items.summary: Agli Arcimboldi di Milano, poi in tuor fino al 25 novembre, “TuttoBrunori” è un live che mescola musica e riflessioni. Sul privato e sull’attualità. “Vorrei raccontare il dubbio, non quello che ti blocca ma quello che anzi ti fa cercare una qualche forma di verità”

deduped_items.title: Guerra ultime notizie. Abu Mazen posticipa elezioni palestinesi all’11 settembre 2027. Iran, Pasdaran: «Attacchi a navi non solo a Hormuz»
deduped_items.summary: Il presidente dell’Autorità Palestinese annulla le elezioni legislative previste per il 28 novembre e fissa una nuova data. I Guardiani della Rivoluzione, i Pasdaran iraniani, hanno annunciato che allargheranno «all’intera regione del Golfo Persico», oltre lo Stretto di Hormuz, le «misure» contro la navigazione «non autorizzata» nell’area. Intanto il presidente del Parlamento iraniano Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf risponde a Rubio: «Vi inginocchierete». A Gaza bambina palestinese uccisa da fuoco isra

deduped_items.summary: Donald Trump apre a un nuovo faccia a faccia con Giorgia Meloni: «Ho un buon rapporto con lei, probabilmente la incontrerò», ha detto rispondendo a una domanda de La Stampa. L’occasione sarà il G20 del 14 e 15 dicembre al Trump National Doral di Doral, in Florida. La dichiarazione è arrivata mentre il presidente americano partiva per il comizio di Syracuse, accompagnato dall’ex campione dei pesi massimi Mike Tyson. Al momento, però, non risulta confermato un bilaterale. Le parole di Trump raffor

deduped_items.title: Terremoto a Panama, crolla il campanile della cattedrale del Cinquecento: le immagini dal drone
deduped_items.summary: Il campanile della cattedrale di San Giovanni Battista crolla dopo la violenta scossa che ha colpito Panama il 9 ottobre. Le immagini dall’alto mostrano i danni al tempio di Penonomé, nella provincia di Coclé, le cui origini risalgono al 1581. Il terremoto di magnitudo 7,6, secondo l’Istituto geologico degli Stati Uniti, ha avuto l’epicentro vicino a Pitaloza Arriba, a 10 chilometri di profondità. Sono seguite decine di repliche e si registrano danni a edifici e strade: finora non risultano vitt
deduped_items.normalised_title: terremoto a panama crolla il campanile della cattedrale del cinquecento le immagini dal drone

deduped_items.title: Il tennista Atmane scaglia la racchetta verso gli spalti: le urla di paura del pubblico
deduped_items.summary: Momenti di paura sugli spalti del Masters 1000 di Shanghai: durante le qualificazioni contro Bernard Tomic, il francese Térence Atmane scaglia la racchetta verso il pubblico dopo un errore sul 2-2 del terzo set. La racchetta colpisce la barriera davanti alle tribune mentre gli spettatori urlano e si scansano: nessuno viene colpito. Atmane riceve una penalità ma non viene squalificato. Poco dopo, sul 5-3 per Tomic, decide di ritirarsi. Il caso arriva negli stessi giorni della squalifica di Daniil
deduped_items.normalised_title: il tennista atmane scaglia la racchetta verso gli spalti le urla di paura del pubblico

deduped_items.title: Cammina davanti all’asilo, poi piomba un drone russo: così si salva per un soffio
deduped_items.summary: Cammina davanti a un asilo quando, all’improvviso, un drone russo piomba dal cielo e provoca una violenta esplosione. L’uomo si accorge del pericolo e riesce a fuggire appena in tempo, mentre una nube di fumo e detriti invade la strada. È successo l’8 ottobre 2026 a Sviatopetrivske, un villaggio alle porte di Kiev, in Ucraina. deduped_items.summary: Il Melonellum, la riforma elettorale tanto voluta da Giorgia Meloni, è diventata legge ieri. Nessun colpo di scena nel voto segreto: tutti i deputati della maggioranza sono stati ligi alle indicazioni. E anche le deputate, nonostante gli appelli al voto di coscienza arrivati fino all’ultimo secondo dalle opposizioni. Ribellatevi, hanno provato a convincerle. Con questa legge elettorale, i capilista bloccati, ossia gli unici che hanno l’elezione già in tasca, non dovranno rispettare alcun equilib

deduped_items.body_text:
Valladolid honra a su Policía Local, «garante de convivencia y seguridad»
La superintendente jefa destaca el rejuvenecimiento del Cuerpo, que cuenta actualmente con «la máxima presencia de mujeres, lo que supone el 16 por ciento de la plantilla»
Valladolid
El Teatro Calderón de Valladolid acogía este sábado la celebración del Día de la Policía Municipal, un acto en el se ha honrado al Cuerpo «garante de la convivencia y de la seguridad en todos los puntos de la ciudad, especialmente en los barrios», destacaba ... el alcalde de la ciudad, Jesús Julio Carnero, quien recordaba que fue «la segunda policía local que se creó en España». Nacida en 1826, el Cuerpo está celebrando este año sus dos siglos de vida, motivo por el que el pasado septiembre se le entregaba la Medalla de Oro de la ciudad.
«Yo tengo que agradecer el trabajo que realizan los 431 efectivos, de los que 72 miembros son mujeres», cuya labor se va adaptando a «las nuevas necesidades que la sociedad va demandando». En este sentido, recordaba la incorporación de tecnología, como la reciente unidad de drones, «que expresa esa actualización y esa profundización que pretendemos llevar a cabo en la Policía Municipal en aras a esa seguridad y convivencia».
La jefa de la Policía Municipal, Julia González Calleja, se refería también al rejuvenecimiento y también feminización del cuerpo. Detallaba que actualmente tiene una media de «40 años aproximadamente» y que estuvo en más de 50, y que, además, cuenta con «la máxima presencia de mujeres, lo que supone el 16 por ciento de la platilla».
La responsable del cuerpo destacaba también la participación del mismo en todos los actos y en el día a día de la ciudadanía, presencia que se ejemplificó con la citada Medalla de Oro que «ha llenado de entusiasmo» a los que forman parte del él.
Asimismo, subrayaba la capacidad de «resolución de problemas, de mediación y de evitar judicializar» del modelo de actuación que tiene.
«Quiero destacar el día a día de la Policía, muy especialmente en los barrios, pero también en los días excepcionales», añadía el regidor, poniendo como ejemplo que los agentes locales se harán cargo de la seguridad durante los días que dure la exposición de la Copa del Mundo en el salón de recepciones del Ayuntamiento, una iniciativa que ha tenido una excepcional acogida como demuestran las colas que está registrando el evento durante toda la mañana.
Carnero, quien presidía el acto, al que asistía en representación de la Junta de Castilla y León el consejero de la Presidencia, Luis Miguel González Gago, concluía su intervención felicitando «a las nuevas promociones, pero también a quienes obtienen algún tipo de condecoración y recompensa». También se acordaba de los miembros del cuerpo que ya están jubilados «y muy especialmente de aquellos que han fallecido».

deduped_items.summary: «La tragedia de lo ocurrido con Maricarmen se tiene que convertir, se ha convertido en fuerza social». deduped_items.body_text:
María Jesús Montero marca la estrategia para ganar las elecciones: «La tragedia de Maricarmen se tiene que convertir en fuerza social»
La líder del PSOE andaluz reivindica el drama del desahucio en Madrid en el gran motor de movilización de cara al 29 de noviembre
«La tragedia de lo ocurrido con Maricarmen se tiene que convertir, se ha convertido en fuerza social». En el PSOE lo tienen claro y lo verbalizó la secretaria general del partido de Andalucía y vicesecretaria general en la Ejecutiva Federal, María Jesús Montero. ... Los socialistas han situado el drama de la anciana de 87 años desahuciada de su piso en el barrio madrileño del Retiro donde vivía desde los 17 años, en el centro de la estrategia política del partido para ganar las elecciones generales del próximo 29 de noviembre.
Arropada por unos 5.000 militantes y simpatizantes en el auditorio Los del Río de Dos Hermanas (Sevilla), en el acto de apertura de la precampaña electoral junto al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, y al alcalde nazareno, Francisco Rodríguez, Montero ha reivindicado que el compromiso asumido por el Ejecutivo para evitar que se repitan situaciones similares convierte a Sánchez en «la garantía de que todo el mundo pueda ejercer sus derechos». Asimismo, ha arremetido con dureza contra la pasividad de la derecha ante los insultos dirigidos a la memoria de Maricarmen Abascal: «Hace tres días el concejal de Benalmádena insultó a Maricarmen y Moreno Bonilla todavía no lo ha cesado», ha afeado la dirigente socialista. El edil popular de la localidad malagueña José Luis Berguillos tuvo que pedir «sinceras disculpas» por llamar «puta sinvergüenza» a Maricarmen antes de su fallecimiento. El PSOE ha pedido su cabeza.
Montero ha enfatizado el peso emocional que tiene arrancar la precampaña electoral en el feudo sevillano de Dos Hermanas, una plaza gobernada por el PSOE desde hace más de cuatro décadas donde se fraguó el renacer de Sánchez. «Gracias, presidente, por volver a elegir Dos Hermanas para iniciar este apasionante viaje a la victoria. Forma parte ya de la historia del PSOE y de la historia íntima del presidente», ha expresado entre ovaciones. Ha agradecido igualmente la gestión del alcalde local y secretario de Organización de la dirección regional, Paco Rodríguez, por consagrar un 45% de los nuevos desarrollos urbanos a Vivienda de Protección Oficial (VPO) para crear «viviendas asequibles para la gente».
«No estás solo»
En una intervención, la interacción con las gradas ha sido una constante. Nada más respaldar al entorno familiar del presidente denunciando «el bulo y la mentira», las miles de personas presentes en el recinto han estallado unánimemente al grito de «¡No estás solo!». Pocos minutos después, al augurar un triunfo rotundo en los comicios del 29-N sosteniendo que «la mayoría social de este país va a ganar las próximas elecciones generales», el auditorio ha respondido coreando con fuerza: «¡Presidente, presidente!».
«Vivimos tiempos complejos, de incertidumbre, nos preocupa esa ola reaccionaria que está recorriendo el mundo, la mala política que practican el señor Feijóo, el señor Bonilla y todos los que le acompañan. En tiempos de incertidumbre necesitamos compromiso, valentía, y si en este país hay un líder con valentía se llama Pedro Sánchez», lo ha ensalzado quien fuera hasta el pasado mes de marzo su vicepresidenta primera del Gobierno.
Políticas sociales frente a «recortes»
Montero ha puesto el acento en las diferencias de gestión económica y social y ha presumido de que el Gobierno progresista ha devuelto «dignidad a los trabajadores subiendo el salario mínimo más de un 60% o convirtiendo sus contratos en indefinidos». Montero ha reprochado que la oposición responda criticando o descalificando. «Gobernar es elegir si se está del lado de la gente o de los que no quieren perder privilegios. Han gritado, lo han insultado y lo han llamado traidor y felón, solo y exclusivamente porque estaba practicando una política que defendía

deduped_items.body_text:
Es la película más vista de Netflix a nivel mundial: un thriller inspirado en hechos reales y con un ganador de Oscar
Lleva dos semanas en el top 1 global y de España y reúne a las estrellas protagonistas de 'Gladiator', 'Peaky blnders', 'Wonder' y 'Divergente'
Las visitas a Netflix se disparan durante el fin de semana. La gente espera hasta sus días de descanso para ver esa miniserie que tiene guardada desde el lunes o esa película que no siempre se puede ver entera de una sentada.
Si eres de los que entran sin un objetivo fijo, esperando a que la plataforma le recomiende esa historia que le deje huella, hoy te traemos una película basada en hechos reales que puede ser la elegida para estos días de pleno octubre.
Se estrenó hace dos semanas directamente en la plataforma de la 'N' roja, sin pasar por los cines, y ya ha conseguido la aprobación del público. Es la película de habla inglesa más vista de Netflix a nivel global y también la más vista en España.
Noticia relacionada
Hablamos de 'Unabomber', el largometraje que ha ocupado el top 1 estas dos semanas. Está dirigido por Janus Metz, conocido por 'Armadillo' y su experiencia con documentales y otras narrativas con el crimen como protagonista.
Trailer de 'Unabomber' en español
Un Premio Oscar y un niño prodigio en el reparto
Antes de revelar la trama de este thriller tan bien acogido por los usuarios de Netflix, queremos destacar al reparto. Los actores hacen de esta película una reunión de talento, premios y taquillazos; en la que el elenco es uno de los motivos que más ha llamado a la audiencia.
Está protagonizada por Russell Crowe ('Gladiator', 'Nuremberg'), ganados de un Premio Oscar por el drama romano del año 2000; Jacob Tremblay ('Wonder'), Annabelle Wallis ('Peaky Blinders', 'Annabelle') y Shailene Woodley ('Divergente', 'Bajo la misma estrella'). La lista de estrellas se completa con Alexander Ludwig, Steven Ogg y Marc Menchaca.
El caso real de 'Unabomber'
'Unabomber' cuenta la historia de Ted Kaczynski, un caso real de un asesino en serie que aterrorizó a Estados Unidos a finales del siglo pasado. El criminal fue un matemático y escritor que envío cartas bomba entre 1978 y 1995 y consiguió 3 víctimas mortales y una decena de heridos por la metralla y la explosión de los paquetes. Murió en 2023 mientras cumplía su pena en prisión.
El nombre hace referencia al mote que le adjudicó el FBI durante su investigación, cuando era un terrorista anónimo. Había atacado una universidad y un avión, y por ello se inventó el nombre 'Unabom', del inglés 'University and Airline Bomber'.
En la película, que dura 1 hora y 40 minutos, se recorre la vida de Unabomber desde sus años en la universidad hasta su detención, 20 años más tarde.
Russell Crowe interpreta a Henry Murray, el psicólogo fundador de la Clínica Psicoanalítica de Harvard que utilizó al futuro terrorista para sus investigaciones cuando era solo un estudiante de la prestigiosa facultad. Jacob Tremblay da vida a Unabomber en su juventud y esos primeros años de deformación moral.

deduped_items.title: Trump administration sanctions International Criminal Court
deduped_items.summary: The United States has announced sweeping sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC), escalating Trump’s war on the international tribunal....
deduped_items.body_text:
Trump administration sanctions International Criminal Court
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
The United States has announced sweeping sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC), escalating Trump’s war on the international tribunal.
“We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling its ability to operate,” US secretary of state Marco Rubio said in an announcement.
The Trump administration has previously pledged to dismantle the court “brick by brick” and has sanctioned 13 current and former staff members, but this is the first time it has levied sanctions against the institution itself.
Ahead of the announcement, prime minister Rob Jetten said the Netherlands will protect the ICC “stone by stone”.
Foreign minister Tom Berendsen said the country would stand behind the court. “The announced sanctions against the International Criminal Court are an undesirable new escalation,” Berendsen said in a statement. “I deeply regret this new step.”
The sanctions will cut the court off from any US company or organisation, including providers of financial and technology services.
The announcement came hours after South African jurist Navi Pillay, who has served as a judge at both the ICC and the International Court of Justice in The Hague, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
Trump has long coveted the prize, telling reporters earlier this week that he deserved the award for what he said was ending eight wars.

deduped_items.title: National Ambulance Service Completes €55 Million Modernization Program
deduped_items.summary: Hungary’s National Ambulance Service (OMSZ) has completed a comprehensive modernization program. With nearly 20 billion forints (55 million euros) in EU funding, the organization has upgraded its infrastructure and equipment, the ambulance service announced on social media. The project focused primarily on modernizing medical equipment. A total of 256 new ambulances have been put into […] The post National Ambulance Service Completes €55 Million Modernization Program appeared first on Hungary To
deduped_items.body_text:
It is capable of transporting necessary equipment and paramedics to the scene even in difficult terrain.Continue reading
Hungary’s National Ambulance Service (OMSZ) has completed a comprehensive modernization program. With nearly 20 billion forints (55 million euros) in EU funding, the organization has upgraded its infrastructure and equipment, the ambulance service announced on social media.
The project focused primarily on modernizing medical equipment. A total of 256 new ambulances have been put into service. The upgrades also include 572 advanced defibrillators with integrated multiparameter ECG monitors and accessories, 234 Doppler devices, 166 standalone ECG machines, as well as other medical equipment and IT infrastructure.
The new equipment is expected to help make prehospital emergency care faster, safer, and higher in quality.
Alongside the completion of the investment program, the OMSZ is continuing its transparency initiative announced in late summer. Since September, the organization has been publishing detailed monthly figures on response times and call volumes on a dedicated online platform.
The data is based on a new calculation method that measures the time from receipt of a 911-equivalent emergency call (112) to the arrival of ambulance crews at the scene. Direct comparisons with older statistics are therefore not possible, as those figures often measured response times only from the moment the ambulance station was alerted.
The latest figures for September present a mixed picture:
- Total call volume (P1–P4): The service recorded 84,963 calls nationwide across priority levels P1 to P4, including 15,903 in Budapest. Compared with August, the number of calls fell 11% nationwide and 5.8% in Budapest, although it remained above the level recorded a year earlier.
- Most critical emergencies (P1): A total of 10,638 calls nationwide were classified as the highest priority. Ambulance crews arrived within 20.10 minutes in 75% of these cases.
In 90% of life-threatening emergencies, paramedics reached the scene within 25.75 minutes. Despite a slight improvement compared with August, the service has yet to meet its own target. In the longer term, it aims to ensure that ambulance crews reach 90% of P1 emergencies within 15 minutes of receiving the emergency call.
Regional figures for September varied. Western Transdanubia recorded the shortest response time nationwide, with crews arriving within 23.16 minutes in 90% of cases. Central Hungary had the longest response time, at 27.75 minutes. Budapest presented a mixed picture. The response time for 75% of calls improved slightly to 19.84 minutes, while the time for crews to reach 90% of incidents increased to 24.89 minutes.
The ambulance service stressed that
response time is an important logistical indicator, but on its own it does not provide a complete picture of the quality of treatment and care.
The organization said it would publish the data in full every month to track progress transparently and document areas where further improvements are needed.
Via MTI, Featured image: MTI/Bodnár Boglárka

deduped_items.title: Hungary Leads Visegrád 4 Countries in Generative AI Use
deduped_items.summary: One-third of Hungary’s working-age population uses generative artificial intelligence, Microsoft’s latest report revealed. This puts the country ahead of its regional neighbors. With the highest rate in the region, Hungary maintains its leading position among the Visegrád countries. According to the international software company’s quarterly Global AI Diffusion report, Hungary (33.3%) ranks 20th globally, ahead […] The post Hungary Leads Visegrád 4 Countries in Generative AI Use appeared first o
deduped_items.body_text:
At the AI Summit 2026, Hungarian media professionals discussed how artificial intelligence is reshaping journalism. Continue reading
One-third of Hungary’s working-age population uses generative artificial intelligence, Microsoft’s latest report revealed. This puts the country ahead of its regional neighbors.
With the highest rate in the region, Hungary maintains its leading position among the Visegrád countries. According to the international software company’s quarterly Global AI Diffusion report, Hungary (33.3%) ranks 20th globally, ahead of Poland (32.3%), the Czech Republic (31.2%) and Slovakia (27.1%).
The share of technology users in Hungary increased by 1.1 percentage points in a single quarter, while Poland recorded an even faster increase of 1.3 percentage points, said Microsoft Hungary in a press release.
Worldwide, 18.8% of the working-age population used generative AI in June, up one percentage point from the first quarter.
The highest rates were recorded in the United Arab Emirates (73.3%) and Singapore (64.3%), with Ireland moving into third place at 49.9%.
Microsoft experts point out that the spread of AI does not in itself mean that the technology will automatically boost productivity or economic performance. To achieve this, companies also need to transform their workflows, train employees, and promote the conscious and responsible use of the technology.
In education, efforts should focus on ensuring that AI genuinely supports learning, the development of critical thinking, and teachers’ work, rather than serving merely as a tool for providing quick answers, the analysts warn.
Microsoft’s annual Work Trend Index, based on a survey of 20,000 AI-using employees across 10 countries, shows that two-thirds of workers fear they will fall behind if they do not adapt quickly with the help of AI. Nevertheless, 45% feel safer focusing on their current objectives rather than using the technology to redesign the way they work.
The statement quotes Barbora Paulovic Deckerova, president of Microsoft’s Central and Eastern Europe and Central Asia region, as saying that
in Hungary, the next phase of AI adoption will be driven less by increasing the number of users and more by improving the quality of how the technology is used.
Microsoft’s Global AI Diffusion report covers 147 economies and estimates the share of generative AI users among the working-age population aged 15-64.
Via MTI, Featured image: Pexels

deduped_items.body_text:
Prague Outperforms Vienna and Berlin in Visitor Ratings
Prague Morning
Prague has received higher visitor satisfaction ratings than Vienna and Berlin, according to the latest Global Tourist Perception Index by Data Appeal Mabrian Intelligence.
The Czech capital scored 92.7 out of 100, compared with 85.6 for Vienna and 78.4 for Berlin, Prague City Tourism (PCT) announced on Thursday.
The results reflect six years of efforts to improve tourism services, visitor experiences and the city’s destination branding, the organization said during International Customer Service Week, held from October 5 to 9.
The Global Tourist Perception Index assesses several aspects of the visitor experience, including hotel satisfaction, safety and tourism products. Prague scored highest among the three capitals, according to PCT.
Visitor spending rises as tourism shifts upmarket
Data from Mastercard transactions indicate that spending by visitors from key foreign markets increased by 18% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year, while the number of visitors rose by approximately 1%.
Social media analysis also points to Prague’s growing association with culture. More than a third of social media posts shared by visitors about the city focused on art and culture, an increase of around five percentage points year-on-year. Nightlife accounted for just 4.5% of reported reasons for visiting, according to PCT.
The Data Appeal Mabrian Intelligence Platform also gave Prague a score of 80 out of 100 for hotel service satisfaction, ahead of Vienna at 75.8 and Berlin at 71.8.
Figures from hotel data provider STR point to further growth in the market. Between January and August 2026, hotel occupancy in Prague increased by 4.9% year-on-year, while the average room rate rose by 5.1%.
Occupancy reached 84.7% in August. According to a recent overview of Prague’s tourism sector by the Czech Institute of Tourism, the average room rate was approximately €123, rising to €170 in the city center and €241 in the luxury segment.
Prague attracts hotel investors
The city is also gaining ground among hotel investors. According to the Cushman & Wakefield Hotel Investor Compass 2026, published in March, Prague ranks among the 15 most attractive European cities for hotel investment, ahead of Vienna, Zurich and Budapest.
Investor interest in Prague’s hotel market has increased for two consecutive years. In the previous edition of the study, the city recorded the largest year-on-year increase in investor interest among the markets surveyed, at 14%. The latest edition showed a further increase of 7%.

deduped_items.body_text:
Prague 7 Turns Streets Into Outdoor Art With Designs by Local Children
Prague Morning
Prague 7 has transformed several streets around local schools with large-scale colorful paintings created with the help of local schoolchildren.
The new artwork can be seen on Rajská, Plynární, Jablonského and Antonínská streets, as well as part of Bubenská Street. The municipality placed the designs mainly near schools and along busy pedestrian routes.
On Antonínská Street, students from grades five through eight at Strossmayerovo Square Elementary School helped create the artwork. They produced the original drawings, which artist Jakub Karlík then combined into the final design.
Several other educational institutions are located close to the painted streets, including Bratrská Elementary School, the Holešovice Business Academy, the Higher Vocational School of Fashion Design and the Secondary Industrial School of Fashion Design.
The new designs have received mostly positive reactions from local residents. Comments on Prague 7’s Facebook page described the streets as more cheerful and said the artwork had made the area more interesting.
There has also been criticism, particularly over the cost and the practical impact of painting the asphalt. Some residents questioned whether the project was necessary and raised concerns about the roughness of the surface, pedestrian movement and whether the paint could become slippery.
Prague 7 said anti-slip paint was used, similar to materials applied to cycle paths and sports surfaces.
The project cost 755,000 CZK, covering the designs, preparation, materials and application. According to Prague 7 spokesperson Martin Vokuš, each of the two phases took around 20 days.
The municipality awarded the contract directly to Karlík. Before selecting his proposal for the Antonínská and Bubenská sections, Prague 7 compared three offers and chose his as the most advantageous.

deduped_items.body_text:
TI Georgia Says ComCom ‘Banned’ Use of 93 Phrases for Government-Critical Broadcasters
Transparency International (TI) Georgia, a local civil society organization, says it identified 93 distinct words and phrases that the Communications Commission, Georgia’s media regulator, “prohibited” government-critical broadcasters from using following last year’s amendments to broadcasting laws, which gave the regulator greater control over TV and radio content.
The watchdog said it identified the phrases after reviewing seven decisions issued by ComCom, a public agency chaired by a former ruling party MP, concerning government-critical broadcasters TV Pirveli and Formula. Both of these channels have been fined several times after the regulator found them in violation of amended broadcasting laws.
“The review found that the Commission prohibits critical broadcasters from using a total of 101 words and/or phrases: 33 in the case of TV Pirveli and 68 in the case of Formula,” TI Georgia said in its October 9 report. In some cases, the words and phrases prohibited for the two critical broadcasters overlap. Overall, the Commission prohibits the use of 93 distinct words and phrases.”
The list includes terms such as “regime,” “prisoners of conscience,” “oligarch,” “false-witness police officers,” “political prisoners,” “political hostages,” “repressive policy,” “Ivanishvili’s prime minister,” “the so-called education reform,” “Georgian Dream police,” “unlawful imprisonment,” “the Scroll-Screenshot Department,” “Georgian Dream government,” “repressive laws,” “the regime’s court,” “Ivanishvili’s president,” “Georgian Dream’s State Security Service,” “judicial clan,” among others, according to TI-Georgia.
In addition to prohibiting specific words and phrases, the watchdog argued that the regulator “requires critical broadcasters to report the news in a dry manner, stripped entirely of commentary and analysis.” According to TI Georgia, the memoranda also identify statements by journalists and presenters that the Commission considers unacceptable, citing several examples.
The watchdog emphasized that it is “deeply concerning” that ComCom “has the power to regulate broadcasters’ content and, on this basis, impose financial sanctions and suspend their broadcasting licenses.” It also argued that, amid what it described as “firmly established and clearly evident state capture in Georgia,” the Commission has for years been composed of commissioners “loyal to and affiliated with Georgian Dream.”
TI Georgia noted that questions remain over the Commission’s decisions and concerns persist that “it has acted to advance the interests of the ruling party and in a biased manner,” warning that “the Communications Commission should not operate as a censor, nor should it be used as a mechanism for punishing critical broadcasters.”
Citing “international practice,” the organization said that “disputed issues should instead be addressed through self-regulatory mechanisms,” and that “promoting and supporting self-regulation should be one of the Commission’s primary objectives — rather than serving the interests of Georgian Dream and penalizing broadcasters for criticizing and exposing representatives of the ruling party.”
The watchdog also warned that the ComCom “continues to act as a censor,” citing its October 1 decision to fine Formula TV GEL 10,000 (USD 3,850) over what the regulator described as violations of impartiality requirements, arguing that the broadcaster’s coverage was based on “personal views.”
“Overall, over the past six months, the Commission has issued formal reports against critical TV channels TV Pirveli and Formula on this same basis seven times – four times against Formula and three times against TV Pirveli,” TI Georgia said.
It added that “most likely,” the ComCom will continue what it called “this harmful practice,” and “will fine TV Pirveli for the same reason. This is because the Commission typically follows a predictable pattern, moving in a

deduped_items.title: OPINION: Sweden's Migration Agency is not fit for purpose. It should be scrapped
deduped_items.summary: An interview by the The Local's Richard Orange with the Migration Agency's legal chief about Sweden’s large number of deportations of British people makes for depressing reading. It demonstrates why the agency is no longer capable of doing its job and now needs to be replaced, argues James Savage.
deduped_items.body_text:
Sweden has deported more British people than any other EU country.
These were people who had moved to Sweden under EU freedom of movement, who had made their lives here, who were often extremely well-integrated and had half-forgotten that they weren’t technically Swedish. People whom the EU and Britain had promised could stay, and who were nonetheless kicked out.
In her interview with Richard Orange, Migration Agency legal chief Susanne Fonsell comes across at times as evasive.
At one point she tries to deflect Richard’s questioning by claiming, hilariously, that she’s “not a specialist” on applying the Brexit migration rules. But if the head of legal at an EU country’s immigration authority is not a specialist on applying EU immigration law, who on earth is?
But the interview was also revealing of the agency’s culture: it sees its job is to be a control agency, not a service agency.
Brits who lived in Sweden prior to Brexit kept rights that were already theirs.
That contrasts with asylum and family reunification, the cases the Migration Agency is used to dealing with, which work the other way round. There, the state grants permission — and in the past decade the state has been turning the screws to make this harder.
It’s clear from her interview that this culture has pervaded all aspects of the agency’s work.
Fonsell also demonstrates a peculiar understanding of proportionality. Under EU rules, her agency was not permitted to deny Brits residency permits if to do so would have been disproportionate. But in response to our question about proportionality she protests that “the legal system must be based on rules and not emotion”.
And so, she seems to effectively dismiss the whole legal concept of proportionality as being a matter of emotions.
If the failures at the Migration Agency were limited to Brexit it would be a short-term problem: incredibly, cases are still emerging, but in a year or two they will stop as Britain’s exit from the EU recedes into the rear-view mirror.
But the incompetence over Brexit is only a symptom of a wider malaise.
For years, The Local has been highlighting the Migration Agency's failures: its staff regularly give incorrect advice to work permit and citizenship applicants, it issues deportation orders over minor admin errors, even when those concerned are willing to correct them.
It repeatedly denies people the right to stay, or even citizenship, for being in Sweden illegally — even when the only reason their permit has expired is that the agency has let their case sit in a pile for too long.
Most Swedish parties want Sweden to limit the numbers of refugees and discourage low-skilled migration. At the same time they actively want high-skilled immigrants. They also have a duty to apply EU law correctly and to give Swedes who fall in love abroad the chance to bring their partners home.
It is clear that the current system is not set up to do all of this at once. The Migration Agency gives shoddy advice, lets cases pile up and then issues rejections on technicalities, even when those rejections are clearly disproportionate. The Migration Courts act as industrial-scale rubber-stampers of agency decisions.
Here, Brexit is an excellent illustrative example: the courts haven’t referred a single Brexit case to the European Court of Justice, despite the fact that important points of EU law are at stake.
Absurdly, the Migration Court of Appeal will only take up cases if they set a precedent, a rule it interprets so narrowly that we are not aware of a single Brexit case that has been heard there.
The agency would presumably point to the fact that it is underfunded. It would also say that it is only applying the law. But how agencies apply the law, how they treat the people that interact with them, is also a matter of culture.
And the culture of the Migration Agency is one of control, when many of its tasks demand a culture of service. The current system is no longer fit for purpose.

deduped_items.title: OPINION: Sweden's Migration Agency is not fit for purpose. It should be scrapped
deduped_items.summary: An interview by the The Local's Richard Orange with the Migration Agency's legal chief about Sweden’s large number of deportations of British people makes for depressing reading. It demonstrates why the agency is no longer capable of doing its job and now needs to be replaced, argues James Savage.
deduped_items.body_text:
Sweden has deported more British people than any other EU country.
These were people who had moved to Sweden under EU freedom of movement, who had made their lives here, who were often extremely well-integrated and had half-forgotten that they weren’t technically Swedish. People whom the EU and Britain had promised could stay, and who were nonetheless kicked out.
In her interview with Richard Orange, Migration Agency legal chief Susanne Fonsell comes across at times as evasive.
At one point she tries to deflect Richard’s questioning by claiming, hilariously, that she’s “not a specialist” on applying the Brexit migration rules. But if the head of legal at an EU country’s immigration authority is not a specialist on applying EU immigration law, who on earth is?
But the interview was also revealing of the agency’s culture: it sees its job is to be a control agency, not a service agency.
Brits who lived in Sweden prior to Brexit kept rights that were already theirs.
That contrasts with asylum and family reunification, the cases the Migration Agency is used to dealing with, which work the other way round. There, the state grants permission — and in the past decade the state has been turning the screws to make this harder.
It’s clear from her interview that this culture has pervaded all aspects of the agency’s work.
Fonsell also demonstrates a peculiar understanding of proportionality. Under EU rules, her agency was not permitted to deny Brits residency permits if to do so would have been disproportionate. But in response to our question about proportionality she protests that “the legal system must be based on rules and not emotion”.
And so, she seems to effectively dismiss the whole legal concept of proportionality as being a matter of emotions.
If the failures at the Migration Agency were limited to Brexit it would be a short-term problem: incredibly, cases are still emerging, but in a year or two they will stop as Britain’s exit from the EU recedes into the rear-view mirror.
But the incompetence over Brexit is only a symptom of a wider malaise.
For years, The Local has been highlighting the Migration Agency's failures: its staff regularly give incorrect advice to work permit and citizenship applicants, it issues deportation orders over minor admin errors, even when those concerned are willing to correct them.
It repeatedly denies people the right to stay, or even citizenship, for being in Sweden illegally — even when the only reason their permit has expired is that the agency has let their case sit in a pile for too long.
Most Swedish parties want Sweden to limit the numbers of refugees and discourage low-skilled migration. At the same time they actively want high-skilled immigrants. They also have a duty to apply EU law correctly and to give Swedes who fall in love abroad the chance to bring their partners home.
It is clear that the current system is not set up to do all of this at once. The Migration Agency gives shoddy advice, lets cases pile up and then issues rejections on technicalities, even when those rejections are clearly disproportionate. The Migration Courts act as industrial-scale rubber-stampers of agency decisions.
Here, Brexit is an excellent illustrative example: the courts haven’t referred a single Brexit case to the European Court of Justice, despite the fact that important points of EU law are at stake.
Absurdly, the Migration Court of Appeal will only take up cases if they set a precedent, a rule it interprets so narrowly that we are not aware of a single Brexit case that has been heard there.
The agency would presumably point to the fact that it is underfunded. It would also say that it is only applying the law. But how agencies apply the law, how they treat the people that interact with them, is also a matter of culture.
And the culture of the Migration Agency is one of control, when many of its tasks demand a culture of service. The current system is no longer fit for purpose.

deduped_items.title: Hostages freed, but Gaza ceasefire’s biggest promises remain unmet
deduped_items.summary: JERUSALEM, Oct 10 — One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-...
deduped_items.body_text:
JERUSALEM, Oct 10 — One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-term promises of the ceasefire have come to fruition.
Here is a list of some of the key points of the October 10, 2025 ceasefire and where things stand:
Hostages released, calm in Israel
Three days after the agreement was announced, Hamas freed the 20 remaining living hostages seized during the group’s October 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest day in Israel’s history.
The captives’ return was a key priority for Israel, whose public had agonised over their fate.
The ceasefire anniversary also marks one year of quiet for Israel from the Gaza front, with no rocket attacks by Hamas.
The group’s missile inventory was depleted by near-constant Israeli bombardment, which damaged or destroyed the vast majority of buildings in the Palestinian territory.
The US military set up a command post with foreign allies near the Gaza border to monitor the truce.
No Israeli withdrawal or let-up
Israel has reduced its level of attacks but has kept striking Gaza on a near-daily basis.
Israeli strikes have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are considered accurate by the United Nations.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is in a tight election race, has vowed to kill everyone involved in the October 7 attack.
Netanyahu said on the attack’s anniversary that 4,000 out of 6,000 “Hamas monsters” had been killed.
Israeli forces were allowed to stay in 53 per cent of Gaza under the terms of the ceasefire, but a year later they control about 70 per cent of it, according to official accounts.
Hamas remains, with weapons
The second phase of the agreement was supposed to include a political transition away from Hamas, and technocrat Ali Shaath was appointed head of a new National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG).
Hamas announced in July that it was disbanding its governing body and handing over Gaza’s administration to the US-blessed NCAG.
But Hamas effectively remains in charge of security in Gaza, and Shaath has taken a low profile.
The Palestinian Islamist movement elected a new leader, Khalil al-Hayya, in July. Shortly afterwards, the group announced it would give up its weapons, a step hailed by Trump as a breakthrough.
But Israel has been sceptical, with Netanyahu demanding verifiable decommissioning of all weapons down to individual guns.
Hamas has not gone ahead with disarmament, and Israel has refused to reciprocate by starting to withdraw forces.
Reconstruction just talk
Trump set up a new global body for the deal dubbed the “Board of Peace”, tapping as key figures former British prime minister Tony Blair and Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov, who serves as “Gaza high representative”.
Trump, a critic of foreign aid, in January promised US$10 billion (RM41 billion) in US funding to the board he controls, and Gulf allies have pledged more, but no money is known to have made its way to Gaza reconstruction.
In September, the board proposed a US$2.45 billion Gaza recovery plan at a meeting of its members and stakeholders, in an effort meant to span over six months. — AFP

deduped_items.title: A year after Gaza ceasefire, families still queue hours for one meal a day
deduped_items.summary: KHAN YUNIS, Oct 10 — Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a com...
deduped_items.body_text:
KHAN YUNIS, Oct 10 — Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting some food for her family.
It has been a year since a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel was supposed to allow food to flood into the ruined territory, yet widespread hunger persists there.
Masri has little choice. Without the kitchen run by humanitarian groups, she and her eight children would have “nothing at all”, the 35-year-old told AFP.
Each day she sets out early in the morning and returns in the afternoon, this time bringing four containers of rice, lentils and a little chicken, which the family throws itself at.
Among them is her husband, wounded in both legs by an airstrike, meaning he “cannot go and fight with the others” to get food.
This will be the only meal of the day for the family of 10, living in a tent in Khan Yunis. There was no breakfast and they will have no dinner.
What little flour they have, Masri explained, has to be rationed.
In August 2025, a United Nations-backed body, the IPC, declared a state of famine in Gaza, though Israel quickly denounced it as a lie.
By December, the UN had lifted that declaration, saying that the ceasefire had allowed in enough supplies over the course of two months to ease conditions.
COGAT, the Israeli defence ministry organisation responsible for civilian affairs in the Palestinian territories, told AFP that the humanitarian situation in Gaza was stable.
But Shaun Hughes, of the UN’s World Food Programme, was less sanguine.
The food security situation, he said, “is still extremely serious”.
The most recent figures, from July, show that “1.4 million out of the population of about 2.1 million people are acutely food insecure”, he said, with 200,000 of them “just one step below famine”.
‘Shameful’
While some food is getting in, a lack of sufficient nutritional variety continues to pose a health threat.
“Dietary diversity is a major food security issue in Gaza,” said Hughes.
“You cannot survive on dry goods and wheat flour and bread alone. Particularly children, particularly pregnant and breastfeeding mothers, they need the micronutrients that come with high protein foods, fresh vegetables, fresh fruits,” he explained.
Masri said that her children, aged between three and 14, “dream of eating fruit” but the family doesn’t have the means to buy any.
She said one of her sons suffered from malnutrition during the 2025 famine, although “little by little, his condition is improving”.
Malnutrition isn’t only caused by a lack of food, but also essential nutrients. It weakens the immune system of children, making them vulnerable to illnesses and stunting their growth.
“Repeated bouts of acute malnutrition amongst children is something that human beings just don’t recover from,” said Hughes.
Cognitive and physical impairments “continue into later life”, he added.
At Khan Yunis’s Nasser hospital, the head of the malnutrition unit, Israa al-Najjar, told AFP she had “observed an increase in syndromes and conditions” linked to malnutrition that affect the immune system.
In a report published on Thursday, the day after the third anniversary of the October 7 Hamas attack that sparked the Gaza war, Medecins du Monde published a study that found 93 per cent of pregnant or breastfeeding women had symptoms of anaemia, which is closely linked to malnutrition.
Just 17 per cent had a sufficiently varied diet to meet their nutritional needs, the group found.
All the while, Masri has kept visiting the community kitchen, despite asthma leaving her exhausted.
Her children spend their days collecting “pieces of nylon, bits of cardboard and chunks of foam” to try and reinforce their tent, which is in a poor state.
She said it was “shameful” that her children had to do so.
“I swear to God, this isn’t normal.” — AFP

deduped_items.title: Hostages freed, but Gaza ceasefire’s biggest promises remain unmet
deduped_items.summary: JERUSALEM, Oct 10 — One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-...
deduped_items.body_text:
JERUSALEM, Oct 10 — One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-term promises of the ceasefire have come to fruition.
Here is a list of some of the key points of the October 10, 2025 ceasefire and where things stand:
Hostages released, calm in Israel
Three days after the agreement was announced, Hamas freed the 20 remaining living hostages seized during the group’s October 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest day in Israel’s history.
The captives’ return was a key priority for Israel, whose public had agonised over their fate.
The ceasefire anniversary also marks one year of quiet for Israel from the Gaza front, with no rocket attacks by Hamas.
The group’s missile inventory was depleted by near-constant Israeli bombardment, which damaged or destroyed the vast majority of buildings in the Palestinian territory.
The US military set up a command post with foreign allies near the Gaza border to monitor the truce.
No Israeli withdrawal or let-up
Israel has reduced its level of attacks but has kept striking Gaza on a near-daily basis.
Israeli strikes have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are considered accurate by the United Nations.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is in a tight election race, has vowed to kill everyone involved in the October 7 attack.
Netanyahu said on the attack’s anniversary that 4,000 out of 6,000 “Hamas monsters” had been killed.
Israeli forces were allowed to stay in 53 per cent of Gaza under the terms of the ceasefire, but a year later they control about 70 per cent of it, according to official accounts.
Hamas remains, with weapons
The second phase of the agreement was supposed to include a political transition away from Hamas, and technocrat Ali Shaath was appointed head of a new National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG).
Hamas announced in July that it was disbanding its governing body and handing over Gaza’s administration to the US-blessed NCAG.
But Hamas effectively remains in charge of security in Gaza, and Shaath has taken a low profile.
The Palestinian Islamist movement elected a new leader, Khalil al-Hayya, in July. Shortly afterwards, the group announced it would give up its weapons, a step hailed by Trump as a breakthrough.
But Israel has been sceptical, with Netanyahu demanding verifiable decommissioning of all weapons down to individual guns.
Hamas has not gone ahead with disarmament, and Israel has refused to reciprocate by starting to withdraw forces.
Reconstruction just talk
Trump set up a new global body for the deal dubbed the “Board of Peace”, tapping as key figures former British prime minister Tony Blair and Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov, who serves as “Gaza high representative”.
Trump, a critic of foreign aid, in January promised US$10 billion (RM41 billion) in US funding to the board he controls, and Gulf allies have pledged more, but no money is known to have made its way to Gaza reconstruction.
In September, the board proposed a US$2.45 billion Gaza recovery plan at a meeting of its members and stakeholders, in an effort meant to span over six months. — AFP

deduped_items.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
deduped_items.summary: RAMALLAH, Oct 10 - Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November due to worsening conditions within the Palestinian territories and set a date of September 11, 2027 for both presidential and legislative elections, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
deduped_items.body_text:
Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
RAMALLAH, Oct 10 - Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November due to worsening conditions within the Palestinian territories and set a date of September 11, 2027 for both presidential and legislative elections, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" to holding elections in November and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections". It called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to participate in the polls.
There had been serious doubts that the Palestinian Authority vote would go ahead in late November. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-06, after which Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas' rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists.
The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections on the previous date.
In Gaza, the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.
Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.
The decision to postpone followed a resolution by the Palestine Liberation Organisation's executive committee and consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process. REUTERS

deduped_items.title: Hostages freed, but Gaza ceasefire’s biggest promises remain unmet
deduped_items.summary: JERUSALEM, Oct 10 — One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-...
deduped_items.body_text:
JERUSALEM, Oct 10 — One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-term promises of the ceasefire have come to fruition.
Here is a list of some of the key points of the October 10, 2025 ceasefire and where things stand:
Hostages released, calm in Israel
Three days after the agreement was announced, Hamas freed the 20 remaining living hostages seized during the group’s October 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest day in Israel’s history.
The captives’ return was a key priority for Israel, whose public had agonised over their fate.
The ceasefire anniversary also marks one year of quiet for Israel from the Gaza front, with no rocket attacks by Hamas.
The group’s missile inventory was depleted by near-constant Israeli bombardment, which damaged or destroyed the vast majority of buildings in the Palestinian territory.
The US military set up a command post with foreign allies near the Gaza border to monitor the truce.
No Israeli withdrawal or let-up
Israel has reduced its level of attacks but has kept striking Gaza on a near-daily basis.
Israeli strikes have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are considered accurate by the United Nations.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is in a tight election race, has vowed to kill everyone involved in the October 7 attack.
Netanyahu said on the attack’s anniversary that 4,000 out of 6,000 “Hamas monsters” had been killed.
Israeli forces were allowed to stay in 53 per cent of Gaza under the terms of the ceasefire, but a year later they control about 70 per cent of it, according to official accounts.
Hamas remains, with weapons
The second phase of the agreement was supposed to include a political transition away from Hamas, and technocrat Ali Shaath was appointed head of a new National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG).
Hamas announced in July that it was disbanding its governing body and handing over Gaza’s administration to the US-blessed NCAG.
But Hamas effectively remains in charge of security in Gaza, and Shaath has taken a low profile.
The Palestinian Islamist movement elected a new leader, Khalil al-Hayya, in July. Shortly afterwards, the group announced it would give up its weapons, a step hailed by Trump as a breakthrough.
But Israel has been sceptical, with Netanyahu demanding verifiable decommissioning of all weapons down to individual guns.
Hamas has not gone ahead with disarmament, and Israel has refused to reciprocate by starting to withdraw forces.
Reconstruction just talk
Trump set up a new global body for the deal dubbed the “Board of Peace”, tapping as key figures former British prime minister Tony Blair and Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov, who serves as “Gaza high representative”.
Trump, a critic of foreign aid, in January promised US$10 billion (RM41 billion) in US funding to the board he controls, and Gulf allies have pledged more, but no money is known to have made its way to Gaza reconstruction.
In September, the board proposed a US$2.45 billion Gaza recovery plan at a meeting of its members and stakeholders, in an effort meant to span over six months. — AFP

deduped_items.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
deduped_items.summary: RAMALLAH, Oct 10 - Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November due to worsening conditions within the Palestinian territories and set a date of September 11, 2027 for both presidential and legislative elections, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
deduped_items.body_text:
Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
RAMALLAH, Oct 10 - Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November due to worsening conditions within the Palestinian territories and set a date of September 11, 2027 for both presidential and legislative elections, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" to holding elections in November and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections". It called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to participate in the polls.
There had been serious doubts that the Palestinian Authority vote would go ahead in late November. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-06, after which Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas' rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists.
The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections on the previous date.
In Gaza, the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.
Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.
The decision to postpone followed a resolution by the Palestine Liberation Organisation's executive committee and consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process. REUTERS

deduped_items.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
deduped_items.summary: RAMALLAH, Oct 10 - Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November due to worsening conditions within the Palestinian territories and set a date of September 11, 2027 for both presidential and legislative elections, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
deduped_items.body_text:
Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
RAMALLAH, Oct 10 - Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November due to worsening conditions within the Palestinian territories and set a date of September 11, 2027 for both presidential and legislative elections, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" to holding elections in November and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections". It called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to participate in the polls.
There had been serious doubts that the Palestinian Authority vote would go ahead in late November. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-06, after which Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas' rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists.
The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections on the previous date.
In Gaza, the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.
Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.
The decision to postpone followed a resolution by the Palestine Liberation Organisation's executive committee and consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process. REUTERS
